_how_to_update: One row per thing a member or club admin can do or will notice. Write it from their side, in plain words: no field names or system detail (that lives in code/ARCHITECTURE.md). Edit here, then run: python3 memberships/coverage/build.py. Fields: area, feature, story, for (member | club | both), phase (Prereq | V1 | V2 | Later | No), prototype (true if it works in the prototype), sweatpals (true if SweatPals has it).

features.story: Members hear at least a day before they're charged: the amount, the date, and a link to manage or cancel.

features.feature: Club chooses how members are reminded
features.story: Club admins pick how early members hear about a renewal and on which channels: the app, email or WhatsApp.
Members get a receipt each time they're charged, with what they paid and when the next renewal is.

features.feature: Failed payment, with a way to fix it
features.story: If a renewal fails, members are told straight away and can pay from a link in the message.
Members hear before the renewal if their AutoPay or card won't go through, so they can update it in time.
Members on an intro offer are told before their first full-price charge.
Anything about money always reaches the member, by email as well, and can't be switched off. Other reminders follow their notification settings.
If the club pauses, changes or cancels a plan, members only get reminders that are still true.

features.feature: Club can see what members were told
features.story: Club admins can check which reminders a member got and when, before answering a complaint.
Pack holders are told before their pack expires, with how many runs are left.
Members who cancelled are reminded when their access ends, with an easy way to rejoin.

features.feature: Daily renewal summary for the club
features.story: Club admins get a short daily note: tomorrow's renewals, payments at risk, and payments that failed.
Members are told when they have one or two bookings left this month.
Members on a paused plan are told when billing starts again.
The plan card shows how much the member has saved this month and since joining.
Each renewal receipt sums up the month: runs, savings and perks used.
Members can book popular events before they open to everyone. Others see when booking opens.
Members get guest passes each month. A friend opens the link and books a run free, and the club gets a new lead.
Club staff can let a guest in with a member's pass at check-in.
Each club has a small page listing its brand offers (gear, food, recovery, nutrition) that anyone can browse and the club can share.
Non-members see the offer and which plan unlocks it. Members tap to reveal the code or how to redeem.
Members can search brands and filter by category.
Clubs can keep some offers hidden until someone joins.

features.feature: Club adds brands and picks the plans
features.story: Club admins add a brand's offer and choose which plans unlock it, and see how many members used it to report back to the brand.
For each plan, club admins choose early access, guest passes and which brand offers it includes.
Clubs can run sessions only plan holders can book.
Joining a plan adds the member to the club's members group.

features.feature: First in line for sold-out events
features.story: When a spot opens, members on the waitlist get it first.
When a friend a member invited joins a plan, the member gets a free week or money off.
Members show a badge on leaderboards, athlete lists and challenges.
Members see their event photos before they're shared publicly.
Members are celebrated for monthly streaks, 25, 50 and 100 runs, and their member anniversary.
Discount codes are off until a club admin turns them on for a plan.
Club admins create a code for a campaign, students or a partner: a percentage or an amount off, on the plans they choose.
A code can take money off the first payment only, or every payment (for example a student rate).
Clubs can cap how many people use a code, set an end date, and switch a code off at any time.
Members enter a code when joining and see the discount as its own line, with a clear message if a code doesn't work.
A code can't be combined with an intro offer.
Clubs can offer a discount only to a group, such as students, women or one company's employees.
Clubs sell a membership that renews every week, month, quarter or year.
Clubs sell a pack of runs that's valid for a set time, or never expires.
A plan can have several price options, such as monthly or quarterly.
New members can pay a lower price for their first weeks, once per person.
Clubs can add a one-time joining fee to the first payment.
Clubs choose which sessions a plan covers: all training runs, race days, or specific events.

features.feature: How often it can be used
features.story: Unlimited, or a set number of bookings a week, month or in total.
Clubs can let unused bookings carry into next month.
For every ticket type, clubs choose what members pay: free, half price, or a custom amount off.

features.feature: Set it once for all events
features.story: When publishing a plan, the club can apply its member price to every upcoming event it covers in one go.

features.feature: Prices shown with tax and fees
features.story: Members see the full price including GST and any fees before they pay.
Clubs pin their main plan to the top and order the rest.
Clubs can hide a plan from the club page and share it by link only.
Clubs can review each request before someone joins, for example a coached squad.
Clubs can stop someone buying the same plan twice.
Clubs can cap how many people hold a plan at once; the plan shows as sold out when full.
Clubs can offer a plan only to people who haven't been to the club before.
Clubs can show a plan only to a group, such as women, students or past attendees.
Clubs can stop selling a plan without affecting people already on it.

features.feature: Plans on the club's own website
features.story: Clubs can show their plans and take sign-ups on their own website.

features.feature: See plans on the club page
features.story: The club page lists its plans with price, what's covered and the perks.
The button always says what will happen: Join, Request to join, Request pending, Not approved, or View if you already have it.
Members choose a price option and whether to take the intro offer.
Members see what's charged today, what renews and when, and any minimum commitment, before they pay.
Members sign the club's waiver and answer its questions while joining.
For approval-only plans, members send a request, pay only once approved, and can withdraw it.
Members see a clear message if a plan is sold out, for first-timers only, already held, or their request was declined.

features.feature: Pay with UPI AutoPay or card
features.story: Members set up AutoPay once and don't have to pay each month.
A confirmation that the plan is active and that benefits apply automatically, with a shortcut to book.
Events show the member price next to the normal price.
People without a plan see what members pay and a link to the plans.
Members book as they do today; checkout uses their plan without any extra step.
When the plan makes a ticket free, there's no payment screen.
Checkout shows which passes the plan covers and which it doesn't.
If a member holds more than one plan, checkout uses the one that costs them least.
The ticket and receipt show the member discount.

features.feature: Run back if you cancel in time
features.story: Cancelling early enough gives the run back to the plan; the club decides how early.
Event pages show which club members are coming.
Members see their plan's status, renewal date, runs left, savings and perks in one place.
Members can see when they joined, renewed, booked and changed anything.
Members can download a receipt for every payment.
Members can update their AutoPay or card from the app or a link.
Members can add their plan to Apple or Google Wallet.
Plans renew automatically on the same date each period.

features.feature: Time to fix a failed payment
features.story: After a failed payment, the plan isn't lost straight away; the club sets how long the member has to fix it.
Members cancel in a couple of taps, or send a request if the club reviews cancellations. The club chooses which.
After cancelling, the plan works until the period already paid for ends. Packs work until they expire.
A member with a failed payment pays it before they can cancel.
Clubs can ask members to stay for a few months before they can cancel; members see this before joining.
Members change plans by cancelling and joining the new one.
Members can come back to a plan any time (without the intro offer again).
Club admins see every plan holder, their status and how much they use the plan.
Monthly income from plans, active holders and failed payments on one screen.
One queue for join requests and cancellation requests.
Club admins pause a plan (an injury, travel); billing stops and the member gets the time back when it resumes.
Club admins can end a plan at the end of the period or straight away.
Club admins can refund a payment and choose whether the plan continues.
Club admins can add bookings to a member's plan for the month.

features.feature: Change a member's price or renewal date
features.story: For one period or from now on.
Club admins send a plan to someone, free, free for a while, or paid, and they claim it from a link.
Club admins see who renews soon and whose payment looks at risk, so they can follow up.
Team-only notes on a member.

features.feature: Who on the team can do what
features.story: Club owners decide who can change prices and refund; staff can check people in and approve requests.

features.feature: Plan money in the weekly payout
features.story: Plan income arrives with the club's weekly payout, like ticket income.

features.feature: Sell a plan at the desk
features.story: Club staff can sign someone up in person and take payment by QR or link.
A member can share their plan with a few people, who claim it from an invite.

features.feature: Club adds people to a plan
features.story: Club admins can add family members to someone's shared plan.
Members pay with a club gift card balance.
Track prospects through stages with automatic messages.
Move existing memberships over from another app.
Plans that cover personal sessions with a coach.
